tool_arguments.query: AWS segment revenue and operating income Q2 2026 Amazon earnings

events.content: AWS segment revenue and operating income Q2 2026 Amazon earnings

Amazon’s latest reported quarter is Q2 2026, released July 30, 2026. [[1]]

| AWS metric | Q2 2026 | YoY comparison |
|---|---:|---:|
| Segment revenue | **$42.2 billion** | **+37%** |
| Segment operating income | **$16.6 billion** | $10.2 billion in Q2 2025 |
| Operating margin | **39.4%** | — |
| Annualized revenue run rate | **$169 billion** | — |

AWS revenue was $42.232 billion, up 37% year over year, while AWS operating income was $16.621 billion versus $10.160 billion a year earlier; the implied/reported segment operating margin was 39.4%. [[1]] [[2]]

**AI contribution:** Amazon did not disclose a separate quarterly dollar revenue or operating-profit contribution from AI within AWS. [[1]] However, management said AWS’s AI business exceeded a **$25 billion annual revenue run rate** and was growing at a **triple-digit year-over-year percentage rate**. [[1]] Amazon also said its chips business—which includes its AI-related infrastructure offerings—exceeded a separate **$25 billion annual revenue run rate**, likewise with triple-digit growth. [[1]] 

At the consolidated level, Amazon reported Q2 operating income of **$27.5 billion**, up from $19.2 billion in Q2 2025, meaning AWS generated roughly 60% of company operating income in the quarter. [[1]] [[2]] Net income of $62.6 billion included **$53.4 billion of non-operating pre-tax other income**, primarily related to Amazon’s Anthropic investment, so that gain should not be interpreted as AWS operating performance or recurring AI operating profit. [[1]]

tool_arguments.query: Microsoft Azure Q2 FY2026 revenue growth AI contribution

events.content: Microsoft Azure Q2 FY2026 revenue growth AI contribution

Microsoft’s latest reported quarter was fiscal Q2 2026, ended December 31, 2025 and released January 28, 2026. [[1]]

- **Azure growth:** Azure and other cloud services revenue grew **39% year over year**, or **38% in constant currency**, versus **40% reported / 39% constant currency** in fiscal Q1 2026. [[1]] [[2]]
- **AI contribution:** Microsoft did **not disclose a separate AI percentage-point contribution** to Azure’s 39% growth in its Q2 materials. It said Azure growth was driven by demand across its services portfolio and continued growth across all workloads, while defining Azure and other cloud services as including cloud and AI consumption-based services. [[3]] [[4]]
- **Broader cloud results:** Intelligent Cloud revenue was **$32.9 billion**, up **29%** year over year, and Microsoft Cloud revenue reached **$51.5 billion**, up **26%**. [[5]]
- **AI demand and constraints:** Management said demand continued to exceed available supply, and noted that efficiency gains in its fungible fleet allowed capacity to be reallocated to monetized Azure demand during the quarter. [[5]]
- **Profitability implication:** Microsoft said Microsoft Cloud gross margin was **67%**, with the year-over-year decline reflecting continuing AI-infrastructure investment and increased AI-product usage, partly offset by Azure and Microsoft 365 efficiency gains. [[5]] 

In short, Azure expanded at a still-exceptional **39% reported growth rate**, but decelerated modestly from Q1; AI is clearly embedded in the growth narrative and infrastructure spending, yet Microsoft did not provide the precise “AI contribution” figure it had disclosed in some earlier periods. [[2]] [[6]]

tool_arguments.query: AWS Q1 2026 revenue and operating income YoY growth AI run rate

events.content: AWS Q1 2026 revenue and operating income YoY growth AI run rate

Amazon disclosed in its Q2 2026 results (quarter ended June 30, 2026) that AWS’s AI business had exceeded a **$25 billion annual revenue run rate** and was growing at **triple-digit year-over-year percentages**. [[1]] 

This represents a meaningful but still partial contribution to AWS: AWS generated **$42.2 billion** of Q2 sales, equivalent to a **$169 billion annualized run rate**, so the disclosed AI run rate equates to **at least 14.8%** of AWS’s annualized revenue base. [[1]] 

The reported AI run rate was also up from **more than $15 billion** in Q1 2026, implying an increase of at least **$10 billion**, or roughly **67%**, sequentially on the disclosed run-rate figures; this comparison is directional because Amazon reported both values as thresholds rather than precise figures. [[2, 1]] 

AWS overall grew **37% year over year** in Q2 2026—its fastest growth in 18 quarters—while management attributed the AI business’s triple-digit growth to the accelerating AI demand wave. [[1]]

tool_arguments.query: AWS Q3 2025 revenue operating income YoY growth AI contribution

events.content: AWS Q3 2025 revenue operating income YoY growth AI contribution

Microsoft’s fiscal Q3 2025, ended March 31, 2025, saw **Azure and other cloud services revenue grow 33% year over year** on a reported basis, or **35% in constant currency**. [[1]] 

AI services contributed **16 percentage points** of that 33% Azure growth—meaning AI was responsible for nearly half of the reported year-over-year growth rate. [[2]] 

For context, Microsoft’s broader Intelligent Cloud segment generated **$26.75 billion** of revenue, up **21% year over year**, while Microsoft Cloud revenue was **$42.4 billion**, up **20%**. [[1]] 

Microsoft also said that scaling AI infrastructure pressured cloud profitability: Intelligent Cloud gross-margin percentage declined despite gross margin increasing $1.9 billion, and cloud/AI engineering investment lifted operating expenses. [[2]]

private_messages.content:
Microsoft’s fiscal Q3 2025, ended March 31, 2025, saw **Azure and other cloud services revenue grow 33% year over year** on a reported basis, or **35% in constant currency**. [[1]] 

AI services contributed **16 percentage points** of that 33% Azure growth—meaning AI was responsible for nearly half of the reported year-over-year growth rate. [[2]] 

For context, Microsoft’s broader Intelligent Cloud segment generated **$26.75 billion** of revenue, up **21% year over year**, while Microsoft Cloud revenue was **$42.4 billion**, up **20%**. [[1]] 

Microsoft also said that scaling AI infrastructure pressured cloud profitability: Intelligent Cloud gross-margin percentage declined despite gross margin increasing $1.9 billion, and cloud/AI engineering investment lifted operating expenses. [[2]]

function.name: finance_research
function.arguments: {"query":"AWS Q2 2025 revenue operating income YoY growth AI contribution"}

private_messages.content:
Amazon’s latest reported quarter is Q2 2026, released July 30, 2026. [[1]]

| AWS metric | Q2 2026 | YoY comparison |
|---|---:|---:|
| Segment revenue | **$42.2 billion** | **+37%** |
| Segment operating income | **$16.6 billion** | $10.2 billion in Q2 2025 |
| Operating margin | **39.4%** | — |
| Annualized revenue run rate | **$169 billion** | — |

AWS revenue was $42.232 billion, up 37% year over year, while AWS operating income was $16.621 billion versus $10.160 billion a year earlier; the implied/reported segment operating margin was 39.4%. [[1]] [[2]]

**AI contribution:** Amazon did not disclose a separate quarterly dollar revenue or operating-profit contribution from AI within AWS. [[1]] However, management said AWS’s AI business exceeded a **$25 billion annual revenue run rate** and was growing at a **triple-digit year-over-year percentage rate**. [[1]] Amazon also said its chips business—which includes its AI-related infrastructure offerings—exceeded a separate **$25 billion annual revenue run rate**, likewise with triple-digit growth. [[1]] 

At the consolidated level, Amazon reported Q2 operating income of **$27.5 billion**, up from $19.2 billion in Q2 2025, meaning AWS generated roughly 60% of company operating income in the quarter. [[1]] [[2]] Net income of $62.6 billion included **$53.4 billion of non-operating pre-tax other income**, primarily related to Amazon’s Anthropic investment, so that gain should not be interpreted as AWS operating performance or recurring AI operating profit. [[1]]

Sources:
[S11.1] Amazon.com, Inc. - Amazon.com Announces Second Quarter Results — https://ir.aboutamazon.com/news-release/news-release-details/2026/Amazon-com-Announces-Second-Quarter-Results/
[S11.2] AMAZON.COM ANNOUNCES SECOND QUARTER RESULTS — https://ir.aboutamazon.com/files/doc_earnings/2026/q2/earnings-result/AMZN-Q2-2026-Earnings-Release.pdf
